key_insight: Wind shear and veer can cut actuator-disk power efficiency by more than 20% because they change both the incoming wind geometry and the rotor’s induction aerodynamics.
engineering_relevance: Wind-turbine power prediction models should account for shear- and veer-driven induction effects, not just rotor-equivalent wind speed, to better estimate performance in realistic atmospheric boundary layers.
method: Concurrent-precursor LES of an actuator disk turbine in stratified atmospheric boundary layers
Controlled inflow LES with shear and veer varied independently
Decomposition of losses into geometric and inductive contributions
evidence_signal: The abstract reports LES results showing statistically meaningful efficiency changes, with shear and veer together reducing power coefficient by more than 20% and each effect approximately linearly superimposing.
watch_item: The findings are based on actuator-disk LES and simplified inflow controls, so translation to fully resolved turbine blades and diverse site conditions may require additional validation.
paper_title: Influence of wind shear and veer on power, thrust, and induction of an actuator disk
